column1: # Compléments aux outils existants (études de notaire, homonymes, tous les doutes, visite aux archives)

column2: Where do I note notary offices and how long they take to reply?
column3: Lists → Archives and sources → 🏛 Notary offices (or ⚖️ Estates → ⋯): each office, its notaries and clerks, its files and its letters. Mark “✓ Reply received” on a letter: after 3 dated replies, the record shows the observed delay, what you have seen, never a legal time limit.

column2: I typed the notary’s name by hand in my files: how do I link them to the office?
column3: 🏛 Notary offices → “🧩 Group them and create their records…”: the app suggests bringing together names that look alike (same surname, same town). Nothing changes before “Apply”, the typed name stays in each file and “↶ Undo” reverses everything.

column2: Why does the “⚠️ Namesakes” alert appear when I write to an heir?
column3: Another record in your database has the same name, born within a few years in the same département: check that you are contacting the right person. “✓ This is the one I am contacting” notes it in the 🕓 Log; “It is not the same person” silences the alert for these two records.

column2: Where can I see all the doubtful points of my family tree at once?
column3: Lists → Research and organisation → ❓ All doubts (or “See all →” in My week): checks, open hypotheses, fragile links, proof disagreements, events without a source. Each line is read from the original tool, nothing is copied; “↗” takes you there and “👁 Mark as seen” sets it aside.

column2: How do I take an archive visit on my phone?
column3: Research → What is missing? → “🗄 Prepare a visit”, then in Lists → Archive visits “📱 Take on the phone”: a single .html file that works without a network. On site, tick what you find, take photos and “⤓ Save my results”; back home, “⤒ Bring back the results” checks the .zip and lets you review it shelfmark by shelfmark.
